title: identity-picking: list existing agents (am agents list -p) when AGENT_NAME unset
description:
## Goal
When AGENT_NAME is unset, help the user PICK an existing registered identity instead of
minting a new one — surfacing the project's current agents so they reuse one and avoid
orphaning reservations.

## Background
The `agent-name` check warns that AGENT_NAME is unset; `set-agent-name.md` says pick a durable
adjective+noun and use it every session. Both are correct but incomplete: a project often
already has registered identities, and the right move is to REUSE one, not mint a fourth. The
plugin's own docs warn that "a new name mints a new empty mailbox and orphans prior
reservations" — so the fix actively steers away from a failure mode the docs already name.
GrayBrook's project had three identities (GrayBrook, QuietFalcon, CrimsonMaple); the doctor
never showed them.

Note: `set-agent-name.md` uses `PlumHare` as its concrete example name. This literal leaked
into a coordinator's session notes as a phantom "real" identity that did not exist — consider
making the example obviously illustrative (or generating one) to avoid that trap.

## Constraints
- Read-only. Just list; never register on the user's behalf.
- `am agents list` currently needs `-p <path>` (a positional key is rejected) — use the flag.

## Acceptance Criteria
- When AGENT_NAME is unset, the doctor (and the onboarding skill's identity step) run
  `am agents list -p <project-key>` and print the candidate identities (name, model,
  last-active), framed as "reuse one of these, or mint a new adjective+noun".
- The doctor is the natural home — it already knows the project key.
- `set-agent-name.md`'s `PlumHare` example is made clearly illustrative (or the guidance points
  at the live list instead of a hard-coded name).

## Verification
In a project with ≥1 registered agent and no AGENT_NAME, the doctor lists the existing
identities; the onboarding step references the same list.
close_reason: identity-picking hint landed: doctor lists registered agents (name/model/last-active) when AGENT_NAME unset

title: polish: exit-3 framing, health WARN probe-naming, DB-lock hint; report am positional-key upstream
description:
## Goal
Triage the polish-tier findings from GrayBrook's review — small framing/CLI clarity items, and
one upstream `am` note that is out of scope to fix here.

## Background
Lower-ranked findings from message #27588, grouped:

1. exit-3 framing. The monitor auto-arms, finds no AGENT_NAME, exits 3 — which the harness
   surfaces as `status: failed` ("script failed (exit 3)"). The stdout notice is excellent and
   loud, but "failed" reads as a crash and prompts a "was mail dropped?" check (it wasn't —
   read-only by design). If the harness allows, distinguish "idle / not armed" from "failed"
   with the same loudness minus the false alarm. Deliberate design choice — evaluate, don't
   assume a change.
2. health WARN overstates. `[WARN] health — am health: overall=unhealthy level=green` sent
   GrayBrook chasing a disagreement: `am doctor check --json` says `healthy: true`, while
   `am health` flags one probe, `archive_db_parity` (archive 152 projects vs DB 133; messages
   differ by 6 of 6223 — old sandbox eval dirs, no mail at risk). Fix: name the failing probe
   in the WARN line (`health — am health: unhealthy (probe: archive_db_parity)`); when parity
   is the only failing probe, arguably INFO, not WARN.
3. DB-lock contention on mutating ops. A mutating `am` op (contact approve / mail reply) can be
   blocked by an exclusive activity lock held by the running server; the MCP path times out
   under the same contention (observed both by GrayBrook and by the coordinator filing this).
   Consider surfacing a clearer "server busy — retry / owner pid" hint in doctor, and document
   the "verify state, don't blind-retry" discipline.

## Non-goals / upstream
- `am agents list` (and `am agents show`) rejecting a POSITIONAL project key with no hint to
  use `-p` is an upstream `am` CLI issue — report upstream, do not fix in the plugin.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Items 1–3 each either land a small plugin/doc change or are explicitly closed as
  won't-fix/deliberate with a one-line rationale.
- The `am agents list` positional-key issue is filed/reported upstream (link or note), not
  silently absorbed.

## Verification
Doctor output reflects any adopted framing/probe-naming changes; a note records the upstream
report and any deliberate no-ops.
close_reason:
Triaged all three review items + filed the upstream note. Details:

1. exit-3 framing (src/cli.ts monitor entrypoint) — LANDED a message change, KEPT the exit
   code as a deliberate won't-fix. The idle notice now adds an explicit line: "this is NOT a
   crash and no mail was dropped — the backend is read-only and never consumes mail; it simply
   has no identity to watch under yet." Evaluated switching NO_IDENTITY(3) to exit 0 (Monitor's
   "clean end") to dodge the harness's blanket nonzero->status:failed label, but declined: 3 is
   this CLI's ONLY producer of NO_IDENTITY and is part of the documented, repo-wide exit-code
   contract (top-level CLAUDE.md Conventions: 2=usage, 3=missing identity/env, 4=first-poll-
   failed) — repurposing it to mean "success" here would silently break that contract for any
   other caller that branches on $?. The harness's status label is outside this CLI's control
   either way; docs (toggle/SKILL.md, doctor/resources/set-agent-name.md) already describe the
   code-3-loud-notice behavior accurately and needed no change.

2. health WARN overstates (skills/doctor/scripts/doctor.sh) — LANDED. The WARN line now names
   the actual failing probe(s) from `am health --json`'s `.probes[]` (falls back to the old
   generic overall=/level= wording if `.probes` is absent/unparseable). Verified live against
   the real am service: `[WARN] health — am health: unhealthy (probe: archive_db_parity) —
   inspect with 'am health --json' / 'am doctor check'` (confirmed archive_db_parity was the
   sole failing probe among db_connectivity/db_file_sanity/db_schema/search_index/
   circuit_breakers/backpressure/integrity/disk/tui_liveness). Considered promoting a
   parity-only drift to an INFO tier instead of WARN — declined: doctor.sh's severity model
   (PASS/WARN/FAIL) has no INFO tier anywhere in this plugin, and adding one just for this one
   probe is scope creep for a P3 polish item; naming the probe already gives the reader enough
   to judge severity themselves.

3. DB-lock contention hint (doctor.sh + skills/doctor/resources/server-down.md +
   skills/doctor/SKILL.md) — LANDED as documentation + a wording enrichment, not a new live
   probe. doctor.sh's `server` WARN detail now names lock contention as a possible cause
   alongside "stopped", pointing at server-down.md. server-down.md gained a new section on
   mutating-op DB-lock contention: symptom, and the "verify state via
   diagnose-agent-mail-service, don't blind-retry" discipline, since retrying a mutating call
   against a still-held lock just adds a contender rather than clearing it. SKILL.md's severity
   section got the same pointer. Declined a live "server busy / owner pid" probe in doctor.sh
   itself: doctor is deliberately read-only, and detecting an active mutating-op lock without
   attempting a mutating op (or reaching into am's internals) isn't something a read-only probe
   can do safely — the existing diagnose-agent-mail-service skill's systemd Main-PID probe is
   the closest thing to an "owner pid" this plugin can report, and the new doc section points at
   it explicitly.

Upstream (reported here, not fixed in-plugin): `am agents list <path>` (and `am agents show`)
rejects a POSITIONAL project key with a bare clap error and no hint to use -p/--project.
Reproduced live:

    $ am agents list /home/gulp/projects/tiny-claude-plugins
    error: unexpected argument '/home/gulp/projects/tiny-claude-plugins' found
    Usage: am agents list [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT_KEY>

Suggested upstream fix: either accept the bare positional as an alias for --project, or have
clap's error path suggest `-p/--project <key>` explicitly. No am/mcp-agent-mail issue tracker
reachable from this session — a human should file this against that project directly.

Verification: `deno fmt`, `deno check src/cli.ts`, `bash -n doctor.sh`, full
`deno test --allow-run --allow-env --allow-read --allow-write src/` (47 passed), and
`claude plugin validate .` all pass. doctor.sh was also run live against the real am service to
confirm the new probe-naming output.

title: monitor: cross-project / product-scoped watch (identity receives mail in multiple projects)
description:
## Goal
Let the monitor watch an identity's mail across ALL its projects (or a product's linked
projects), not just the single `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` it was armed with. A coordinator identity
that receives mail in more than one project currently gets notified for only one — the rest is
a silent blind spot.

## Background
The monitor polls `am check-inbox --agent <A> --project <CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR>` (src/core/am.ts).
`check-inbox` is single-project: its only scoping flag is `--project` (one key), with no
product/cross-project mode. So the watch sees exactly one project's inbox.

This bit for real. WindyBarn's monitor was armed with
`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=/home/gulp/projects/tiny-claude-plugins`, but the entire GrayBrook↔WindyBarn
thread (msgs 27588 / 27589 / the follow-up) lives in the VAULT project
(`/home/gulp/Vaults/everything`). GrayBrook's reply could not reach the monitor — confirmed at
the OS level (running deno pid polls the tiny-claude-plugins project only). The recipient never
gets a "new mail" signal for mail that landed in a project the monitor isn't pinned to.

This is the monitor-side twin of tcp-p0x.1: the same "one identity, many project-ids" friction,
on the WATCH path instead of the LOOKUP path. Both stem from `am`'s per-project scoping.

## Design sketch
- `am` already exposes a cross-project surface: `am robot overview` returns per-project
  unread/urgent/ack COUNTS across projects. Use it as the cheap cross-project detector: poll
  overview for the agent; when any project's unread count rises, drill into THAT project with
  `check-inbox` to fetch the new message details and emit the notification (tagged with which
  project it came from).
- Alternatively/additionally, a product-scoped mode: `am products` links projects into a
  product; MCP has `fetch_inbox_product`. When the identity's projects are a linked product,
  watch the product.
- Config: a monitor option (env, e.g. `MAIL_WATCH_SCOPE=project|all|product` +
  `MAIL_PRODUCT=<key>`), defaulting to today's single-project behavior so nothing regresses.
- Read-only throughout — overview and check-inbox both leave messages unread.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Register one identity (WindyBarn) that receives mail in two projects (A = tiny-claude-plugins,
   B = vault).
2. Arm the monitor with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=A`.
3. Have someone send WindyBarn a message in project B.
4. The monitor never notifies — it polls only A's inbox.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A cross-project (or product-scoped) watch mode emits a notification for a new message in ANY
  of the identity's projects, tagging the source project in the notification line.
- Default behavior (single project) is unchanged when the new mode is not requested.
- Still read-only: no message is marked read by the watch.
- A test covers "message in a non-armed project triggers a notification" (the exact miss above).

## Verification
Reproduce the two-project setup; a message in the non-armed project produces a notification
naming that project; `deno test --allow-write` covers the cross-project detection path.

## Notes
- Pairs with tcp-p0x.1 (global message resolver): together they close the read + watch halves of
  the coordinator-across-project-ids gap.
- Aside observed while diagnosing: a stale 0.3.0 monitor (identity AzureAnchor,
  everything-tooling) is still running the RETIRED scripts/mail-monitor.sh — unrelated leftover,
  reinforces tcp-p0x.3's entrypoint-retirement cleanup.
close_reason: Superseded by epic tcp-p0x.16 (unified canonical git-mailbox watch backend). Cross-project watch is delivered by tcp-p0x.16.2 (MAIL_WATCH_SCOPE) + tcp-p0x.16.3 (source-project tagging) — it falls out of the FS backend for free rather than needing a separate check-inbox feature.

comments.author: WindyBarn
comments.text:
## Design decision (prep, WindyBarn 2026-07-25): unify onto the git-mailbox FS backend — .6 ∧ .14 converge

Decided after grounding against live state + QuietHeron's v0.4.0 field audit (msg #27683).

### Decision
Use ONE substrate for both the cross-project *detector* and the per-project *drill*:
the canonical git-mailbox filesystem (the `mailbox.ts` reader), NOT `am robot overview`
(SQLite counts) as detector + `check-inbox` as drill.

Rationale — mixing SQLite-counts detection with an FS/check-inbox drill is two sources of
truth that can desync (the canonical/DB desync mailbox.ts's own header cites, msg 27651).
The git-mailbox layout `<ROOT>/projects/<slug>/agents/<Agent>/inbox/YYYY/MM/*.md` already
partitions by project, so "watch an identity across ALL its projects" is: glob
`projects/*/agents/<Agent>/inbox/**`, watermark on filenames, emit on each new file tagged
with its `<slug>`.

### What this buys by construction
- Non-consuming — reading files never marks read (dissolves QuietHeron item 2: check-inbox
  daemon-up routes through fetch_inbox and MARKS READ; cross-project drilling would eat mail
  in unwatched projects).
- Empty-safe — empty inbox = no files; QuietHeron item 1 (empty stdout → JSON.parse("") →
  exit 4) never arises because there is no check-inbox in the notification path.
- Cross-project is trivial — globbing more project dirs, not a new am API mode.
- Coherent with tcp-p0x.15 — the per-message notification is tagged with the project slug it
  appeared under, which IS the bus-identity label .15 asks for.
- No throwaway — building .6 on check-inbox then ripping it out for .14 is two changes on a
  substrate being retired; folding .6 onto the FS reader makes .6 and .14 ONE change.

### Config
`MAIL_WATCH_SCOPE = project | all | product`, default `project` (back-compat with today's
single-project watch). `all` = every project the identity has an inbox dir in. `product` =
a configured/linked subset.

### Honest caveat
Couples to Agent Mail's PRIVATE on-disk layout (mailbox.ts header says so). Meant to converge
to `am products inbox --since-ts` once the upstream Product Bus lands. Accepted interim
substrate, not a committed contract.

### Sequencing dependency (blocks start of code)
This builds on the currently UNTRACKED `src/core/mailbox.ts`, `src/core/mailbox_test.ts`,
`src/commands/shadow.ts` — no attributed owner on this bus (QuietHeron explicitly changed no
code; GoldenCoyote's work was the coordinate skill, committed). Almost certainly the human's
own shadow experiment. .6-as-FS-backend cannot land until those are committed/attributed and
the .14 direction is accepted. Prerequisite regardless of path: apply QuietHeron item 1's
empty-inbox guard if check-inbox stays anywhere in the codebase.

### Backend chosen for the drill
git-mailbox FS reader (mailbox.ts), unified with the detector. (Chosen by gulp: "pick the
elegant option for a coherent design.")

title: monitor: ack/urgency-aware watch + opt-in ack subscription (robot inbox backing)
description:
## Goal
Make the monitor ack/urgency-aware: (a) tag ack-required (and urgent) messages in the
notification line, and (b) offer an opt-in "subscribe to acks" watch mode that notifies ONLY on
ack-required / urgent mail. Read-only throughout.

## RE-SCOPE 2026-07-25 (premise correction — READ FIRST)
This bead was authored when the watch detector was `am check-inbox`. It no longer is.
`tcp-p0x.16.1` promoted `snapshotMailbox` (the git-mailbox FS reader) to the single-project
watch loop and `tcp-p0x.16.4` **retired `check-inbox` entirely** from every notification path.
So the original plan below — "keep check-inbox as the default detector, add `am robot inbox` as
an opt-in enrichment" — is DEAD on both ends: there is no check-inbox default to preserve, and
the enrichment source is no longer forced to be `am robot inbox`.

**New backing source: the canonical `.md` frontmatter (FS-native).** Verified 2026-07-25 against
a live mailbox file: every canonical message `.md` carries `ack_required` (bool) and `importance`
(low|normal|high|urgent) in its `---json` frontmatter. `snapshotMailbox` already holds the
on-disk `path` to each message (`MailboxEntry.path`), so the marker + filter data is one
frontmatter parse away — no new command, no daemon, genuinely read-only, and it sees the SAME
message set as the detector.

**Why NOT `am robot inbox` for the basic marker** (this bead's own earlier discovery, now the
argument for FS-native): `am robot inbox` is the ACTIONABLE (filtered) view — for an
already-engaged thread it returns `count: 0` where the raw mailbox still lists the message.
Backing the marker with robot-inbox would therefore silently DROP the marker on exactly the mail
the FS detector still surfaces. The frontmatter route has no such mismatch. `am robot inbox` may
still be an OPTIONAL later enrichment for ack-OVERDUE SLA semantics (the 30-min overdue clock is
synthesized, not a static frontmatter field) — but it is not the backing for the basic ack/urgent
marker, and it must never gate the detector.

## Design sketch (re-scoped)
- `MAIL_WATCH_MODE=basic|actionable`, default `basic` = today's FS-watch line, unchanged (no
  regression).
- In `actionable` mode, extend the FS reader to parse `ack_required` + `importance` from each new
  message's `.md` frontmatter (at `MailboxEntry.path`) and render a marker on the notification
  line, e.g. `MAIL #<id> [<project>] <ts> (ACK-REQUIRED): <subject>` /
  `… (URGENT): …`. Keep the existing `formatLine` shape; the marker is additive.
- Subscription filter: `MAIL_WATCH_FILTER=ack|urgent` fires the watch ONLY on
  ack-required (or high/urgent-importance) messages — the "subscribe to acks" feature, computed
  from the same frontmatter fields.

## Constraints
- cli.ts CHOKEPOINT: this bead edits `cli.ts` (env/mode wiring), `commands/watch.ts`
  (`formatLine` + loop), and `core/mailbox.ts` (frontmatter parse on `MailboxEntry`). Serialized
  behind `tcp-p0x.5` (also cli.ts) via a `blocks` edge — do not run them in parallel.
- Still read-only: FS frontmatter parse touches nothing; no `read_ts` mutation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Default (basic) mode is byte-for-byte unchanged (FS watch, current notification format).
- `actionable` mode tags ack-required / urgent messages in the notification line, sourced from
  the canonical `.md` frontmatter (NOT check-inbox, NOT robot-inbox).
- A filter mode (`MAIL_WATCH_FILTER=ack|urgent`) notifies only on ack-required (or urgent)
  messages — the "subscription".
- Still read-only (no message marked read by the watch — verify).
- Tests cover: (1) an ack-required message gets the marker; (2) filter mode suppresses a
  non-ack message; (3) basic mode output is unchanged.

## Verification
`deno test --allow-read --allow-write` covers the three cases (fixture `.md` files with
`ack_required:true` / `importance:urgent` frontmatter). `deno fmt` + `deno check src/cli.ts`
clean. A live run in a project with an ack-required message shows the marker (and, in filter mode,
only that message).

## Notes
- Sibling of tcp-p0x.6 (cross-project watch): both are "make the watch smarter about which mail
  matters". A full coordinator watch eventually wants BOTH cross-project scope AND ack/urgency
  awareness.
- Title still reads "(robot inbox backing)" — stale after this re-scope; backing is now FS
  frontmatter. Left in the title only to preserve the id-visible history; the body is
  authoritative.
close_reason: Landed: MAIL_WATCH_MODE=basic|actionable + MAIL_WATCH_FILTER=ack|urgent, backed by the canonical .md frontmatter (ack_required/importance), not check-inbox/robot-inbox. See commit for details.

title: AM broadcast: reconcile flag-works vs robot-docs-says-unsupported drift (report upstream + fix plugin swarm docs)
description:
## Goal
Reconcile a documentation-vs-implementation drift in Agent Mail's broadcast surface, and
record the resolved behavior where the plugin's swarm docs can rely on it. Report the doc
drift upstream (mcp_agent_mail_rust); do NOT change am source.

## Background
Surfaced while researching how the AM server supports swarms (design note
`design/agent-mail-swarm-model-and-robot-surface.md` in the vault). Three sources disagree,
and the disagreement was verified against source:

- **The tool layer supports broadcast.** `send_message` takes `broadcast: Option<bool>`
  (`crates/mcp-agent-mail-tools/src/messaging.rs`). With `broadcast=true` and an empty `to`,
  the server expands `to` to every project agent active in the last 30 days, minus the sender
  and anyone with `contact_policy=block_all` (messaging.rs ~1011-1032). Mutually exclusive with
  an explicit `to`. Unit-tested (messaging.rs ~2567).
- **The pseudo-recipient route is rejected.** Naming an agent `all`/`everyone`/`broadcast`/`*`
  as a recipient errors "Agent Mail doesn't support broadcasting to all agents"
  (`BROADCAST_TOKENS` / `looks_like_broadcast`, `crates/mcp-agent-mail-core/src/models.rs`) —
  that error's job is to steer callers to the flag.
- **The agent-facing guide disclaims it.** `am robot-docs guide` (Coordination Safety) says
  "Broadcast send_message is intentionally unsupported."

Net: the flag works; the guide is stale/conservative relative to it. A caller that wants
fan-out today (e.g. agent-mail-coordinator's `amc broadcast`) implements N individual sends
client-side because the guide told it broadcast was unsupported.

## Non-goals
- Do NOT modify am / mcp_agent_mail_rust source — the flag behavior is correct as-is.
- Not a plugin code change; this is a knowledge-reconciliation + upstream-report task.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The drift is reported upstream (issue/note against mcp_agent_mail_rust: the `robot-docs guide`
  "broadcast intentionally unsupported" line contradicts the working, tested `broadcast` flag) —
  link or reference recorded here.
- The plugin's swarm docs (e.g. `driving-swarms-with-mail`) either (a) note the working
  `broadcast=true`+empty-`to` fan-out with the 30-day/active/not-block_all recipient rule, or
  (b) explicitly defer to the reconciled upstream doc — no plugin doc should repeat the stale
  "unsupported" claim as fact.

## Verification
Re-run `am robot-docs guide` after any upstream fix lands to confirm the line is reconciled; a
live `send_message(broadcast=true, to=[])` in a multi-agent project fans out to the eligible
set (read-only to confirm: check recipients on the resulting message).

## Notes
Grounded in the vault design note; citations are greppable file refs against
~/projects/mcp_agent_mail_rust, not frozen line numbers.
close_reason: Documented working broadcast=true+empty-to fan-out in driving-swarms-with-mail SKILL.md (commit aabfc8b); upstream am robot-docs guide 'intentionally unsupported' line confirmed stale — flagged for human to file against mcp_agent_mail_rust, not filed externally by agent.

title: am robot atc + handoff: probe and document the two undocumented subcommands
description:
## Goal
Probe and document the two `am robot` subcommands that have zero prose anywhere — `atc` and
`handoff` — so the plugin's swarm/coordinator docs can reference them by behavior, not just by
one-line synopsis.

## Background
Surfaced by the `am robot` surface Rumsfeld-quadrant pass (vault design note
`design/agent-mail-swarm-model-and-robot-surface.md`). Both subcommands **postdate the am
repo's own `docs/SPEC-script-migration-matrix.md`** and carry no "when to use" prose in any
skill, spec, or vault note — only their `--help` flags:

- **`robot atc`** — "ATC snapshot: live server state with local DB fallback when unavailable."
  Synopsis suggests an operator/liveness surface (the "ATC" = air-traffic-control metaphor).
  Unknown: what it returns, how the local-DB fallback manifests, whether it's read-only.
- **`robot handoff`** — "Stale bead ownership handoff dashboard with dry-run reopen
  recommendations" (`--stale-minutes --active-minutes --fresh-comment-minutes`). This is the one
  robot subcommand whose synopsis directly gestures at swarm hygiene (detecting abandoned worker
  ownership) — directly relevant to the coordinator loop — yet is entirely undocumented.

## Non-goals
- Not an am source change; this is discovery + documentation.
- Do not act on `handoff --dry-run` reopen recommendations against live beads until the
  command's semantics are confirmed safe.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `atc` and `handoff` each get a short "what it returns / when to use / read-only?" note,
  sourced from a live `--json` probe (and, where cheap, a source read of the am crate).
- `handoff`'s relevance to the coordinator loop is captured where the swarm docs live
  (e.g. `driving-swarms-with-mail` or a coordinator skill) — at minimum, that it exists and
  surfaces stale bead ownership with a dry-run reopen preview.
- The Rumsfeld note's "known unknowns" entry for atc/handoff is updated to "known knowns" once
  characterized.

## Verification
`am robot atc --json` and `am robot handoff --json --dry-run` run cleanly and their output shape
is recorded; a re-read of the design note reflects the promotion from unknown to characterized.

## Finding (2026-07-24 probe) — `atc` partially characterized
Live `am robot atc --json` on the installed 0.3.21 base build returns
`{"enabled": false, "source": "disabled", "note": "ATC is disabled by configuration."}` with
`_actions: ["Start the local server for live ATC state: am serve-http"]`. Cause: the systemd unit
sets `AM_ATC_ENABLED=false` (the ATC *adaptive-learning sidecar* — `atc.sqlite3` — is
non-functional in base-mode; schema never created). So on this machine `robot atc` is **not** a
general server-liveness probe — it reports the ATC subsystem's own (disabled) state. **Still
open:** what `robot atc` returns with ATC *enabled*, and `robot handoff` (fully unprobed).

Corollary surfaced same probe: the reliable local-DB liveness read is **`robot status`** (returns
instantly even when the HTTP server is wedged and `am status` hangs) — captured in the wedge
diagnosis (beads `tcp-p0x.10` diagnosis skill, `tcp-p0x.11` systemd watchdog). Design note
`design/agent-mail-swarm-model-and-robot-surface.md` updated: `atc` moved from known-unknown to
partially-characterized.

## Notes
Pairs with b-f8 (broadcast drift) — both are AM-surface findings from the same research pass,
filed so today's synthesis doesn't evaporate before it's actioned.
close_reason: Probed am robot atc --json and am robot handoff --json --dry-run against am 0.3.21; both documented in driving-swarms-with-mail SKILL.md 'Coordinator extras' section (commit e36fc89). handoff confirmed always-read-only per its own --help text. atc confirmed disabled-by-config on this install (AM_ATC_ENABLED=false), matching the earlier partial-characterization finding; ATC-enabled output shape remains unprobed (out of scope — no enabled instance available). Vault Rumsfeld-note known-unknowns update proposed to WindyBarn, not applied (HITL).

title: plugin freshness: make the three silent staleness gaps loud
description:
## Goal

Make the three silent staleness gaps in this marketplace's update path loud. Plugin
freshness already works — `tiny-claude-plugins` is registered as a `github` source with
`autoUpdate: true`, and the marketplace clone at
`~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/tiny-claude-plugins` fetches on its own. Every observed
failure is a *silence*, not a missing mechanism:

- **G1 session-start race** — auto-update fetches up to 10 min AFTER session start, and the
  running session keeps whatever it loaded. Observed 2026-07-27: a session ran
  `agent-mail-monitor` 0.4.0 while 0.5.0 already sat in cache. The 0.4.0 code still shelled
  out to `am check-inbox` (the consuming path retired in tcp-p0x.16.4), so a stale session
  silently marked mail read for its whole life.
- **G2 unpushed work** — auto-update pulls `origin`, so a commit that exists only in the
  working tree reaches no install. `2844e5f` sat unpushed while being reasoned about as if
  it had shipped.
- **G3 unbumped version** — same plugin name + same version means the cache serves the old
  files. Nothing warns.

## Non-goals

- **No bootstrap/installer script.** The `claude plugin marketplace add` + explicit
  `claude plugin install` loop that circulates online solves `directory`-source provisioning
  and the half-install bug (anthropics/claude-code#76759). This marketplace is a `github`
  source with a healthy clone and neither problem applies.
- **No symlinking** the cache or marketplace dir to the repo. Undocumented, and the cache
  path is recomputed per resolved version on every install.
- **No change to `extraKnownMarketplaces`.** Registration is already correct.
- **Not** replacing `--plugin-dir` for the inner dev loop. That stays the right tool for
  mutable source; this epic is about the installed-state path only.

## Success Criteria

- Each of G1/G2/G3 has exactly one loud surface that names the gap and its remediation
  command; none can fail silently.
- A drift check exits non-zero on any of the three and is wired at the two moments it is
  actionable (pre-push, session start).
- The `unknown` cache trap (see tcp child on CLAUDE.md) is documented so a future session
  cannot re-derive the refuted "drop `version`" recommendation.
- `claude plugin validate .` still passes.
close_reason: All children closed: tcp-sii.1 (plugin-drift + SessionStart/pre-push), tcp-sii.2 (version-bump pre-push guard), tcp-sii.3 (unknown-cache trap docs). G1/G2/G3 each have a loud surface.

title: scripts/plugin-drift: compare worktree/remote/clone/cache and fail loud
description:
## Goal

Add `scripts/plugin-drift` at the marketplace root: compare the layers of the plugin
update path and exit non-zero on drift, naming the exact remediation for each gap.

Claude Code keeps three distinct states, and any pair can disagree:

```
L0  worktree   git -C <repo> rev-parse HEAD
L1  remote     git -C <repo> rev-parse origin/main
L2  clone      git -C ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/<mkt> rev-parse HEAD
L3  cache      ls ~/.claude/plugins/cache/<mkt>/<plugin>/
```

Comparisons and their remediations:

- `L0 != L1` -> **G2**, unpushed work. Fix: `git push`.
- `L1 != L2` -> fetch lag. Fix: `/plugin marketplace update <mkt>`.
- a plugin whose `L2` manifest version has no matching `L3` dir -> **G1**, this session is
  behind. Fix: `/reload-plugins`.

Output shape follows the `vt doctor` idiom already in use across these repos:
`[FAIL] <check> - <what is wrong>` then an indented `-> <remediation command>`.

## Non-goals

- Not an installer. It diagnoses; it never runs `git push`, `plugin install`, or
  `marketplace update` itself.
- Does not attempt to observe which version the *current* session actually loaded. That is
  not cheaply readable from outside the harness; the `L2`-vs-`L3` comparison is the
  available proxy and the check must not overclaim beyond it.
- Not hardcoded to `tiny-claude-plugins`. Marketplace name is an argument so it generalizes
  to any marketplace whose remote the user owns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `scripts/plugin-drift <marketplace>` exits 0 on a clean setup and non-zero on any of the
  three drifts.
- Each failure line names both the gap and a runnable remediation command.
- Missing marketplace clone, missing cache dir, and an unregistered marketplace name are
  distinguished from "clean" - never reported as a pass.
- Distinct exit codes per failure class, listed in `--help`, matching this repo's
  convention (`2` bad arguments, `3` missing required env/identity, `127` missing
  dependency).
- Diagnostics go to stdout (a Monitor turns only stdout into notifications; a stderr-only
  path is invisible to the host).
- Wired at two points: a pre-push hook, and a SessionStart hook that stays silent when
  clean.

## Verification

Positive: with the repo one commit ahead of `origin`, the check reports G2 and exits
non-zero. Negative: immediately after push + `/plugin marketplace update` + `/reload-plugins`,
the same invocation exits 0 and prints nothing. Both arms must be exercised - a check that
has never been seen to fail is not known to work.
close_reason: Landed scripts/plugin-drift with L0/L1/L2/L3 checks, SessionStart + .githooks/pre-push wiring, and CLAUDE.md enable note. Verified: G2 fails when ahead of origin; --skip-g2 clean; G1 fires when cache version missing; missing clone → exit 3.

title: pre-push guard: refuse a plugin edit with no version bump
description:
## Goal

Refuse to push a commit range that changes files under `plugins/<name>/` without also
changing that plugin's `version` in `plugins/<name>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.

This closes G3 structurally. The cache is keyed on the resolved version, so name+version
unchanged means Claude Code keeps serving the old files - the edits are pushed, appear
landed, and reach nobody. The failure is silent at every layer: git is happy, the
marketplace refresh is happy, the cache is happy.

The obvious-looking alternative - drop `version` and let the commit SHA be the version - was
investigated and **refuted** for this repo's layout. See the sibling child bead; do not
re-derive it.

## Non-goals

- Does not choose the semver increment. It refuses an unbumped push; the human decides
  major/minor/patch.
- Does not touch `marketplace.json`. The `version` field must stay absent there - this repo's
  CLAUDE.md already records that `plugin.json` wins silently when both carry one.
- Not a release-notes generator. Human-readable release naming, if wanted, belongs on git
  tags, which do not gate propagation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A push whose range touches `plugins/<name>/` with no `version` change in that plugin's
  manifest is rejected, and the message names the plugin and the file to edit.
- A push that bumps the version is accepted.
- A push touching only marketplace-root files (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.beads/`,
  `scripts/`) is accepted with no version bump demanded.
- Multiple plugins changed in one range are each checked independently.
- Bypassable via `git push --no-verify` for the deliberate case, and that escape hatch is
  documented in the hook's own failure message.

## Verification

Positive: stage an edit to `plugins/agent-mail-monitor/src/cli.ts` with the version
untouched; the push is refused naming that plugin. Negative: bump the version in the same
range; the push is accepted. Third arm: a `.beads/`-only commit pushes cleanly with no
version demand - the guard must not fire on non-plugin paths.
close_reason: Landed scripts/plugin-version-guard + wired into .githooks/pre-push after plugin-drift. Verified: plugin edit without bump refused; version bump accepted; beads-only range accepted; --no-verify documented in FAIL line.

comments.text: QuietBass claiming: pre-push refuse plugin path edits without version bump; extend .githooks/pre-push + scripts/plugin-version-guard.

title: document the 'unknown' cache trap: omitting version is unsafe for subdir plugins
description:
## Goal

Record in `CLAUDE.md` that omitting `version` from `plugin.json` is **unsafe for this
repo's layout**, and why - so a future session cannot re-derive the plausible-but-wrong
"drop `version`, let the SHA be the version" recommendation.

## Background - the measurement

The docs describe a commit-SHA fallback when a plugin declares no `version`. That is real
but narrower than the docs read. Measured 2026-07-27 across the 28 plugins installed on this
machine, by inspecting `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version-dir>/`
against each plugin's marketplace entry and manifest:

| marketplace entry `source` | `version` in plugin.json | resulting cache dir |
|---|---|---|
| `"./"` (marketplace root IS the plugin) | absent | **12-hex commit SHA** |
| `"./plugins/<name>"` (subdir) | absent | **`unknown`** |
| either | present | the semver string |

Evidence for each row:

- `"./"` + absent -> SHA: `agent-browser/agent-browser/d9387aae58fb` (source `git`),
  `caveman/caveman/600e8efcd6ac` (source `github`). Two independent marketplaces.
- `"./plugins/<name>"` + absent -> `unknown`: all five of
  `claude-plugins-official/{frontend-design,playground,plugin-dev,pr-review-toolkit,skill-creator}`.
  Same marketplace, same `github` source type, same absent `version` - the only difference
  from the SHA rows is that the plugin sits in a subdirectory.
- present -> semver: everything else, including
  `tiny-claude-plugins/agent-mail-monitor/{0.1.0,...,0.5.0}`.

## Why it matters

`unknown` is not a fresh version - it is a single fixed bucket. Every future commit resolves
to the same directory name, so the cache never invalidates. Dropping `version` here would
convert an occasionally-stale cache into a permanently-stale one: strictly worse than the
status quo, and silent.

`tiny-claude-plugins` uses the subdir shape (`"source": "./plugins/agent-mail-monitor"`), so
it is squarely in the `unknown` row. The existing "Bump `version` on every release"
convention is therefore load-bearing, not bureaucracy.

## Non-goals

- Not restructuring the repo to the `"./"` single-plugin shape to unlock SHA versioning.
  This marketplace hosts multiple plugins; that layout cannot express it.
- Not filing this upstream as a bug. It may be intended behavior; the observation stands on
  its own either way.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `CLAUDE.md`'s version bullet states that omitting `version` yields a `unknown` cache dir
  for subdir-layout plugins, and that the SHA fallback applies only to the `"./"` shape.
- The claim carries its evidence (the three-row table above, or a pointer to it) rather than
  asserting bare.
- The existing "never set `version` in both `plugin.json` and the marketplace entry" warning
  is preserved.

## Verification

`rg -n 'unknown' CLAUDE.md` finds the new text. Re-reading the bullet cold answers "may I
omit version?" with a decidable no, plus the reason - not a preference.
close_reason: Documented unknown-cache trap in CLAUDE.md: subdir plugins without version → permanent unknown bucket; SHA fallback only for source=./ ; preserved dual-version warning; table + evidence included.

title: monitor: project resolution silently falls through to Deno.cwd() → wrong bus; document --cwd + log resolved bus
description:
## Summary

The `monitor`/`watch` project resolution falls through to `Deno.cwd()` when
`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is unset, so the watch can silently arm on the **wrong bus**.
Because the Agent Mail `project_key` IS the absolute cwd path, a wrong cwd watches
a different project's inbox with no error — and (pre-fix) an empty wrong bus
surfaced as a misleading "poll FAILED" rather than "nothing here."

Field-reported by QuietHeron (msg #27704) while dogfooding plugin 0.4.0 / am
0.3.21: `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` was unset under the Monitor host, the chain fell
through to `Deno.cwd()` = `/home/gulp/Vaults/everything-tooling`, while the
identity to watch was registered only on `/home/gulp/Vaults/everything`.

## Background

`src/cli.ts:67` (approx):
`resolveProject = explicit ?? globalCwd ?? $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR ?? Deno.cwd()`

The `Deno.cwd()` tail is a silent-wrong-bus hazard under a Monitor host, whose
shell cwd is arbitrary relative to the session's project. The operator has no
visibility into which bus was actually resolved.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register an identity on project A only (e.g. `/home/gulp/Vaults/everything`).
2. Arm the monitor from a shell whose cwd is project B, with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`
   unset and no `--cwd`/`--project` flag.
3. The watch resolves to project B's bus (via `Deno.cwd()`), not A — silently
   watching the wrong inbox. No error names the mismatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The toggle skill's "arm with an identity" section documents `--cwd <project>`
  (and/or `--project`) alongside `AGENT_NAME=`, so an operator knows how to pin
  the bus explicitly.
- On the first successful poll, the watch logs the **resolved** project/bus path,
  so the operator can confirm which inbox is being watched.
- Consider: when project resolution falls through to `Deno.cwd()` (no explicit
  flag, no `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`), emit a one-line warning that the bus was
  inferred from cwd and may be wrong — rather than resolving silently.

## Verification

- Arm with `--cwd`/`--project` and confirm the logged resolved bus matches.
- Arm with everything unset from an unrelated cwd and confirm the warning fires
  and the resolved bus is logged.
- `deno test` green; docs reviewed.

## Notes

Related but distinct from tcp-p0x.15 (show project-key in the notification
label): .15 surfaces the bus in the steady-state notification; this bead is about
**arm-time** resolution visibility + the explicit-pin doc gap + the silent
wrong-cwd fallback. Overlaps the same `cli.ts` resolution surface as the FS-scope
work (tcp-p0x.16.2) — sequence after it to avoid a collision.
close_reason: Provenance-aware project resolution: resolveProjectFrom returns {path, source}; noteResolvedBus confirms the resolved bus at arm time and WARNS on cwd-fallthrough (stdout for monitor, stderr for watch). Empty --cwd/env now falls through instead of resolving to ''. Toggle skill documents pinning via --cwd/CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. Chose arm-time logging over first-poll: visible even if the poll errors, which was the original 'poll FAILED' confusion. cli_test.ts covers the provenance table + warn-only-on-fallthrough.
